samples.summary: Release can arm canvas shortcuts while an in-place text box is still mounted (keepalive-exemption is per-control, not per-session)
samples.evidence: The hook only exempts the control that currently holds focus (`el.closest('[data-text-edit-keepalive]')`, toolbar-focus-release.ts:71). But the docs text-box session's lifetime is decided elsewhere: `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751` commits ONLY on the hidden textarea's blur, and skips the commit when `relatedTarget` is keepalive. So once focus has legitimately parked on a keepalive control (e.g. the Font size `<input>` inside the keepalive wrapper, packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-size-picker.tsx:144-181), the session stays mounted and the textarea will never blur again. Clicking any plain, non-keepalive toolbar button that is still rendered during text-edit (e.g. Undo in `UndoRedoGroup`, Format painter, zoom controls — all mounted alongside `TextEditSection` in packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:111-117) moves focus keepalive-input → plain button, which does NOT commit, and the new hook then blurs to `document.body`. From that point `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:174-178` (Delete/Backspace) and the arrow-nudge / printable-key type-to-edit rules pass their only gate (`!isEditableTarget(e.target)`), because no rule consults `editor.isTextEditing()` / `getEditingElementId()` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:2284). Delete would then remove the very element whose text box is open. Fix belongs on the new hook: also skip the release while `editor.isTextEditing()`.

samples.summary: Issue #882 still reproduces from the slides side panels / mobile toolbar, which are not opted into the release
samples.evidence: The gate being worked around is document-wide (`isEditableTarget` sees any focused `<button>`, packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:177), but only the desktop `<Toolbar>` carries `data-canvas-toolbar`. Plain buttons in the slides side panels keep focus after a click and re-engage the same gate: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/background-side-panel.tsx:130,174,186,193,218 (also theme-panel.tsx / theme-builder-panel.tsx, and `MobileSlidesToolbar` at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/mobile-toolbar.tsx:94, which has no opt-in and is what an external-keyboard tablet gets). Nothing in the change or the design doc records the panels as an accepted gap the way board is recorded.

samples.summary: Existing per-picker `releaseFocusToBody` wiring is now redundant/duplicated by the hook
samples.evidence: Four slides toolbar consumers still wire the old point fix `useMenuCloseHandlers(releaseFocusToBody)`: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/shape-controls.tsx:60, border-picker.tsx:72, text-element-controls.tsx:62, table-controls.tsx:103 (plus fill-picker/gradient-editor.tsx:307). With the toolbar root now opted into `useCanvasFocusRelease()`, the swatch-close path blurs twice and the repo carries two overlapping mechanisms for the same contract; nothing marks which one is now authoritative.

samples.summary: Opt-in is an untyped literal attribute on the root, so the `CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR` constant and its only real consumer can drift silently
samples.evidence: `Toolbar` is a plain `div` spread (packages/frontend/src/components/ui/toolbar.tsx:11-26), so `data-canvas-toolbar=""` at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110 is a hand-written string with no compile-time link to `CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR` (packages/frontend/src/components/toolbar-focus-release.ts:33) — and packages/frontend has no `tsc` lane at all, so even a typed helper would not be checked. The only thing tying them together is the new test; a future toolbar that copies the pattern (mobile toolbar, board) has no typed affordance to get it right.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end in the repo. The new hook's keepalive exemption is evaluated only against the element that currently holds focus (toolbar-focus-release.ts:66-74), but the docs text-box session ends only on the hidden textarea's blur (docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751), and that blur already happened when focus moved to a keepalive control (font-size-picker.tsx:144-181, which focuses the input on pointerdown and only re-focuses the editor when a value actually changes — font-size-picker.tsx:71-88, text-edit-section.tsx:73-80). Plain non-keepalive buttons are mounted alongside TextEditSection (slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110-138) and have no mousedown preventDefault (global-controls.tsx:54-60), so focusing one satisfies isReleasable() and the hook blurs to document.body. From body, the document-level keydown listener (slides editor.ts:2727-2729) runs rules gated only by !isEditableTarget (keyboard.ts:214-230, 871-890), which no longer blocks, and the selection is the element under edit (editor.ts:3970) — Delete/Backspace removes the very element whose text box is still mounted. The only other session exit is a canvas pointerdown (editor.ts:3532-3547), which a toolbar click never reaches, so no existing guard closes the path. This is squarely blast-radius: a new guard with a reachable bypass through entry points not in the diff.
